gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement is a plain sans with rounded, parenthesis-like forms. Its tall middle band makes lines look stocky and dense as text keeps going, a sturdy follow-up to the closed, bent-straw letters of Plakkaat.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption is a plain sans with big-bodied lowercase. Its bowls stay unclosed and inviting, so paragraphs of text feel open, while Plakkaat holds the page with closed, single-weight letters.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-mro: Hairline wire on top, dense tall text below. Quantum is best at thin, rope-like outlines with loose spacing, while Noto Sans Mro is best at dense, tall-in-the-middle words with generous entrances.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Quantum keeps its y tail as thin as its arm. It is best at loose, spacious display lines, while Noto Sans Myanmar does better at thick, heavy-looking strips of text with a broad, welcoming c.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-nabataea: Thin wire tubing, tall sturdy text. Quantum stays loose and wire-like while Noto Sans Nabataean stands nearly cap-tall with generous s curves, making the two feel like thread beside type.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-newa: Thread-thin and spacious, Quantum looks drawn in one unswelling line of ink, with no taper anywhere. And Noto Sans Newa sits beside it fuller, with an open e and tall bowls.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu is a plain sans with a towering x-height. Quantum does best with uniform-width, wire-like curves and loose spacing, while the body font does best with terminals held far from the stroke.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Clean and steady, Quantum feels drawn with a technical pen. The best thing here is how Noto Sans Ol Chiki packs words into solid blocks, with curve tails held back, against the loose lines of Quantum.
